t.6.107.1: Having heard these auspicious words, so well spoken by Rāghava, Maheśvara uttered this still more auspicious speech.
t.6.107.2: O lotus-eyed one, mighty-armed and broad-chested scorcher of foes, by good fortune this deed has been accomplished by you, O best of those who bear weapons.
t.6.107.3: By good fortune, O Rāma, the dreadful darkness that had grown over the whole world, the fear born of Rāvaṇa, has been dispelled by you in battle.
t.6.107.4: Having consoled the sorrowful Bharata and the illustrious Kausalyā, and having seen Kaikeyī and Sumitrā, the mother of Lakṣmaṇa,
t.6.107.5: O mighty one, having obtained the kingdom in Ayodhyā, having gladdened your circle of friends, and having established your line in the family of the Ikṣvākus,
t.6.107.6: Having performed the horse sacrifice and attained unsurpassed glory, and having given wealth to the brāhmaṇas, you ought to go to heaven.
t.6.107.7: O Kākutstha, here stands King Daśaratha, your father, seated in a celestial chariot, he who was your illustrious guru in the world of men.
t.6.107.8: The glorious one, delivered by you, his son, has gone to the world of Indra. Together with your brother Lakṣmaṇa, you should salute him.
t.6.107.9: Having heard the words of Mahādeva, Kākutstha, together with Lakṣmaṇa, made obeisance to his father, who stood upon the summit of the celestial chariot.
t.6.107.10: Together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, the lord beheld his father, blazing with his own splendour and clad in spotless garments.
t.6.107.11: Then King Daśaratha, standing in his aerial chariot, was filled with great joy on seeing his son, who was dearer to him than his own life-breaths.
t.6.107.12: The mighty-armed lord, seated on an excellent seat, took him onto his lap and embraced him with both arms; then he began to speak.
t.6.107.13: Bereft of you, O Rāma, neither heaven nor the honour bestowed on me by the gods and seers is esteemed by me. This I truly pledge to you.
t.6.107.14: O best of speakers, the words that Kaikeyī spoke to bring about your banishment remain lodged in my heart.
t.6.107.15: But having seen you safe and well and having embraced you together with Lakṣmaṇa, today I am freed from sorrow, like the sun freed from the mist.
t.6.107.16: O son, I have been delivered by you, a worthy and great-souled son, just as the righteous brāhmaṇa was delivered by Aṣṭāvakra.
t.6.107.17: And now, O gentle one, I understand how the lords of the gods have appointed the Supreme Person here for the slaying of Rāvaṇa.
t.6.107.18: Truly fulfilled in her purpose is Kausalyā, who, filled with joy, will behold you, O Rāma, returned from the forest and come home, O slayer of foes.
t.6.107.19: Fortunate indeed, O Rāma, are those men who will see you, returned to the city, wet with the waters of consecration and anointed as lord of the earth.
t.6.107.20: I would wish to see you united with Bharata, who is devoted, strong, pure, and walks in the path of dharma.
t.6.107.21: O gentle one, fourteen years have been spent by you dwelling in the forest together with Sītā and the wise Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.107.22: Your dwelling in the forest has come to an end, and your vow has been made fruitful. And by slaying Rāvaṇa in battle, those gods have been gladdened.
t.6.107.23: You have accomplished a praiseworthy deed and won glory, O slayer of foes. Established in the kingdom together with your brothers, may you attain a long life.
t.6.107.24: As the king was speaking thus, Rāma, with joined palms, said: “O knower of dharma, be gracious to Kaikeyī and to Bharata.”
t.6.107.25: O lord, that terrible curse with which you addressed Kaikayī, saying, 'I abandon you together with your son,' may it not touch Kaikayī and her son.
t.6.107.26: Having said "So be it" to Rāma, who stood with joined palms, the great king embraced Lakṣmaṇa and spoke these words once more.
t.6.107.27: By devotedly serving Rāma together with Sītā, the princess of Videha, you have brought me great joy, and the fruit of dharma has been won by you.
t.6.107.28: O knower of dharma, you will attain merit and vast fame on earth, and, with Rāma pleased, heaven and greatness as well.
t.6.107.29: Serve Rāma, O enhancer of Sumitrā's joy, may good fortune be yours; Rāma is ever devoted to the welfare of the whole world.
t.6.107.30: These three worlds together with Indra, the Siddhas and the supreme sages, approaching the great-souled one, worship him, the Supreme Person.
t.6.107.31: This is that which has been declared the unmanifest, the imperishable, fashioned by Brahman, the heart of the gods and their secret, O gentle one: Rāma, the scorcher of foes.
t.6.107.32: By you, who served Rāma with devotion together with Sītā, the princess of Videha, the merit of righteous conduct and vast fame have been attained.
t.6.107.33: Having spoken thus to Lakṣmaṇa, who stood with joined palms, the mighty-armed king, righteous of soul, spoke auspicious words to Vaidehī.
t.6.107.34: But, O Vaidehī, you must not feel resentment over this rejection; Rāma, who wishes your welfare, did this for the sake of your purification.
t.6.107.35: O fair-browed one, you need not be instructed regarding service to your husband; yet I must surely say this: he is your supreme deity.
t.6.107.36: Having thus instructed his two sons and likewise Sītā, his daughter-in-law, Daśaratha, blazing with splendour, went to the world of Indra in his aerial chariot.
